exposure: duration of the second stage of labour
mode of delivery (operative delivery, trial of labour past limits, spontaneous vaginal delivery)
outcome: composite maternal morbidities (postpartum hemorrhage, infection, fever >=38degC, abdominal organs injury, anal sphincter injury, relaparotomy, maternal intensive care unit admission)
cohort: The study participants were nulliparous women with a singleton, viable, term fetus in a cephalic presentation who were in the second stage of labour.
finding: Extending the second stage of labour beyond 2 hours (or 3 hours with epidural) in nulliparous women was associated with increased maternal morbidity compared to a shortened second stage leading to 100% operative delivery or spontaneous vaginal delivery within standard time limits.
mod_finding: Both 100% operative delivery within standard time limits and spontaneous vaginal delivery within standard time limits were associated with lower maternal morbidity compared to extending the second stage of labour.
